title: The Prophet at Ta'if
hookLine: stoned out of the town of Ta'if, the Prophet refuses to curse its people and prays for their descendants
last: EVEN IF YOUR SINS REACHED THE CLOUDS.

lines: A ROAD OUT OF A HILL TOWN.
cards: A road leading away from a hill town, and a man walking it, hurt and slow. Behind him, a crowd is still shouting. He had come to Ta'if to speak to its leaders.

The early biographies say they refused him, then set people along the road to jeer as he left; some tellings add stones. He reaches the shade of an orchard and sits down. This is the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him.
What happens further down that road, as he later told it himself, is today's story.

teach.b: In a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, his wife Aisha asks whether he ever faced a day harder than the battle of Uhud.

He says his people had hurt him badly, and the worst was the day he went to Ibn Abd Yalil, a chief of Ta'if, and was turned away. He walked on so troubled that he only came to himself further down the road.
He looks up and sees a cloud, and in it the angel Gabriel, who says God has heard how the people answered him, and has sent the angel of the mountains.
That angel greets him and offers, if he wishes, to bring the mountains together on the town. A complete answer to everything that just happened. He says no.
In paraphrase, he hopes God will bring out from their descendants people who worship God alone. Not a curse. A hope, aimed at children not yet born.
The people who drove him out are left standing, and their grandchildren get a future in his words.
A word on sources: the jeering crowd comes from the sira, the early biographies.
The angel and the answer come from the hadith. Muslim teachers tell it as a picture of mercy at the very moment the power to answer was in his hands.
He had been humiliated, he was offered the means to settle it, and he chose the longer view.

how: Muslims tell the story of Ta'if, from the hadith and the early biographies, as an example of the Prophet's mercy; teachers use it when speaking about answering rejection without revenge.

o: the city where the Prophet was born
the hill town that turned the Prophet away
the oasis town where he later settled

games.q: the Prophet at Ta'if — tap the pairs.
p: the town that turned him away

s: the Prophet asked God to punish the people of Ta'if
he refused the angel's offer and hoped for their descendants instead.
the angel and the refusal come from a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari
Aisha reports him telling it; the crowd on the road comes from the sira.

games.q: you're on the road back from Ta'if, bruised and shaken. an angel offers to bring the mountains down on the town. what do you say?
o: no. maybe their children will worship God.
games.why: he said no, and hoped God would bring from their descendants people who worship God alone. not a curse: a hope for children not yet born.

practice: Bring to mind one person, or one group, who turned you away: a job that said no, a friend who closed the door, a family that didn't make room.
Without replaying the scene, try a wish that reaches past the hurt, that things go well for them, or for the people who come after them.
If you pray, you can pray for them in your own tradition's words; if you don't, just hold the wish.

wordCard.voice: Ta'if. The town that drove the Prophet out; offered the mountains against it, he gave its children a hope instead. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Ta'if, the hill town that turned the Prophet away.
